- [2023/05/23] The user is interested in the evolution of Minerva's worship and mythology in Rome.
- [2023/05/23] Minerva was originally an Etruscan goddess of wisdom, trade, and handicrafts before being adopted into the Roman pantheon.
- [2023/05/23] During the Republic era, Minerva became associated with war and Roman military strength.
- [2023/05/23] In the Imperial era, Minerva was elevated to a major deity associated with the emperor and the empire.
- [2023/05/23] Minerva's worship included festivals such as Minervalia (March 19), Quinquatria (March 19-23), Consualia (August 21), Minerva Medica (October 3), and Saturnalia (December 17-23).
- [2023/05/23] The Temple of Minerva on the Capitoline Hill was built in the 6th century BCE and was significant during the early Republican era.
- [2023/05/23] The Temple of Minerva Chalcidica, built in the 5th century BCE, was located near the Circus Flaminius and featured a statue by Phidias.
- [2023/05/23] The Temple of Minerva on the Aventine Hill was built by Domitian in the late 1st century CE.
- [2023/05/23] Temples dedicated to Minerva were often decorated with statues, frescoes, and mosaics and served as civic and cultural centers.
